Those palpitations are constant, almost, and they're driving me absolutely insane.

I guess what brings me in is just the sheer exhaustion of dealing with this every single day. I've lost my job because of it. My manager keeps asking if I can come in, and I have to explain that I feel terrible, dizzy, and like I might pass out at any second. It's not fair. feedback_history.therapist_response:

That sense of being seen as a threat to your own stability—that must feel so isolating. And the fact that you’re trying to protect yourself by not taking medication that might help, even though it’s been hard, shows how deeply you care about your safety and your dignity.

Imagine if I could just be myself at work, or even just walk through my neighborhood without half my family members checking their watches or asking if I need water because I looked like I was going to faint. feedback_history.therapist_response:

And it’s so important that you’re feeling this deeply, because when someone says, “I’m here,” it’s not just about words—it’s about showing up with your whole self, even when your body feels like it’s trying to pull away. That’s not weakness. That’s courage.  

Would it be helpful to explore, together, what might help you feel a little more grounded in your body—without having to take medication that feels like it’s adding more pressure? Maybe we can start with something gentle, something that feels safe to try.

feedback_history.patient_message:
Yeah, that makes so much sense. I've been thinking about exactly that. The idea of trying something "gentle" and "safe" sounds terrifyingly simple, but honestly, it's the only thing keeping me from just giving up completely.

I don't want to take Propanolol yet. You know why? Because my blood pressure is already on the lower side, usually around 100/60. And last time I tried an SSRI, even though it was supposed to help with anxiety, it made me feel like I was going to faint multiple times. It felt like someone turned the volume knob all the way up on my dizziness. So, I'm scared that another pill might just make that wall between who I am and how I show up even thicker.

But... maybe we could try a grounding technique first? Something physical that doesn't involve chemicals? Like deep breathing or maybe just focusing on one sensation
feedback_history.therapist_response:
Of course—I’m here with you, and I won’t rush it. Let’s try this slowly and gently, just like you asked.  

Close your eyes if that feels comfortable, or keep them open if you’d prefer. Take a slow, deep breath in through your nose—let your belly rise, like it’s filling with air. Don’t rush it. Just let your breath move in and out, like a quiet rhythm.  

Now, when you exhale, let it go slowly through your mouth—like you’re blowing out a candle. Feel your chest soften, your shoulders drop. Just stay with the breath. No need to change anything. If your chest feels tight or your head spins, just pause and bring your focus back to the breath.  

We’ll do this together—just one breath, then the next. And when you’re ready, we can go slower or stop anytime.  

Would you like to start with that first breath now?
